attempts.note: The smallest positive integer is 1, not 3.

attempts.reason: In the product with a single U(1) bundle on Σ, every PS representation in one generation is tensored with the same space of zero modes, so all gauge representations have the same multiplicity M.  The Pati-Salam (and SM) one-generation content is already anomaly-free; copying it M times remains anomaly-free for every integer M.  There is no condition that forces M=3.  (Relative fluxes for different representations are not part of this product: they would be an extra choice, and even then anomaly cancellation constrains linear combinations, not a unique M=3, and is not derived from the locked conoid.)

attempts.attempt: KO-dimension or the real structure J
attempts.reason: KO-dimension of Y × F is 2+2+6 ≡ 2, independently of the choice of connection on Σ.  J is the product real structure and does not see the integer flux.

attempts.attempt: Tadpole / equation of motion for the background flux
attempts.reason: There is no string-theory tadpole condition in the spectral action of Y × F_PS; imposing one would be an import from a different framework, not derived here.  The Maxwell equation d * F = 0 is satisfied by a constant flux on T² or a monopole on S², for every integer M.  That is quantization plus a classical solution, not a selection of 3.

attempts.attempt: Matching the tip length 8ℓ0 or C4 to the torus lattice

coincidences.flag: numerology / unprincipled: the tip circle is a boundary of the conoid factor, not a cycle of the torus factor.  There is no identification of those circles in the product metric.

The C4 of the locked conoid rotates the conoid's angular coordinate, not a coordinate of Σ.  The product isometry group is C4(X) × Isom(Σ).  Requiring Isom(Σ) to contain a C4 (i.e. τ=i, up to SL(2,Z)) is a symmetry wish, not a consistency condition of the product, and even then it fixes at most the shape of T², not the flux.
coincidences.match: C4 is an isometry of the square torus τ=i

coincidences.flag: numerology, already rejected in doc 47; the 12-bridge spacing is a convention

attempts.attempt: Identify |∫_X K dA| / 2π = 1 with the flux on Σ
attempts.flag: Even as an identification, this would give flux 1, not 3.  Treating the curvature of the conoid as a flux on a different factor is not forced by the product connection.

attempts.S2: On S² the local small-t expansion is the same in structure: the leading volume term 4π R² / (2π t), a curvature term fixed by χ=2, and a monopole term that costs energy ~ n² / R².  The distinguished bundles (Hopf, n=1; tangent, n=2) are not n=3, and the energy cost prefers smaller |n| at fixed R.  We do not invent an exact monopole-harmonic spectral action beyond this local argument and the index n.
attempts.analytic_reason: The exact heat kernel is |M| coth(2π t |M|/A) = A/(2π t) + (2π t M²)/(3A) + O(t³).  The first M-dependent term is positive and minimized, at fixed area, by the smallest |M|.  The Weyl term A/(2π t) grows with A.  For a positive cutoff function the spectral action therefore prefers smaller |M| and has no interior minimum at M=3.  τ does not enter the spectrum of a constant-flux Dirac operator on a flat torus, so this action cannot fix the complex structure either.
attempts.attempt: Minimization of the magnetized-T² spectral action over (M, A)
attempts.wilson_lines: A common Wilson line is a translation and does not change eigenvalues.  Relative Wilson lines among several stacks are not present in a single-bundle product; they would be an extra choice and affect Yukawas, not the Dirac spectrum of one bundle.

flux_mechanisms.headline: Nothing in the combined geometry fixes the flux to 3, or uniquely fixes the area, complex structure, or Wilson lines of Σ.  The spectral action of a magnetized torus prefers smaller |M|, not M=3, and does not depend on τ.

divergences.int_R_Y_for_S2: diverges: Area(X) * 8π → ∞, plus a finite piece Area(S²)*(-4π)
divergences.int_R_Y_for_T2: finite: Area(T²) * ∫_X R_X → -4π Area(T²), because T² is flat
divergences.note: C0 is the finite part of Area(X) after subtracting π b² and the log term.  It does not make vol(Y) or the flux Yang-Mills integral finite for M ≠ 0.

gauge_BCs.verdict: derived, assuming the CCvS spectral action on Y × F_PS

option_A.description: N_F = 3 as an input of F_PS; Σ may be flux-free

option_B.description: N_F = 1; three chiral zero modes from flux M=3 on Σ
option_B.generation_count: equal to M, and M is not derived (see flux_mechanisms)
option_B.reason: CCvS compute the Higgs/σ potential from traces on a finite Dirac operator whose generation index already sits in D_F.  In option B the generation index is a zero-mode label on Σ, and the Yukawas are overlap integrals.  Those traces are not the CCvS ones.  We do not invent a replacement a4 computation.

generations.preferred_for_this_survey: option_B, with option_A recorded only as the literature PS model

gravity.reason: The local Einstein-Hilbert coefficient is fixed only once the cutoff moments are chosen, and it lives on Y, not automatically in observed spacetime.  C0 and ∫K enter integrated terms and do not uniquely determine the moments.
gravity.verdict: failed to uniquely derive G_N (or even G_Y) from the product

higgs_sigma.verdict: The CC2012 σ-extension can accommodate a 125 GeV Higgs after running, as a literature result with free parameters.  The product geometry does not uniquely predict m_H.  In the flux-generation setup the CC2012 traces do not apply off the shelf.

verdict_headline: The product Y × F_PS with Y = (truncated conoid) × Σ is a consistent 4D, KO-dimension-2 almost-commutative geometry.  The Pati-Salam gauge relations at Λ are derived (spectator).  Nothing in the combined geometry fixes flux = 3 or the moduli of Σ.  The one-loop (and partial two-loop) RG pipeline determines (m_R, Λ) from measured couplings; it does not predict those couplings.  Yukawa moduli are not uniquely fixed; a labelled fit is underdetermined.  The Higgs mass is not a unique prediction of the product.

principled_scan.tau_not_in_the_dirac_spectrum: As already used in flux_mechanisms: the Dirac eigenvalues on a flat magnetized torus are independent of τ, so the spectral action of D_Σ cannot be the principle that fixes τ.  Any remaining principle would have to come from an a4 Yukawa potential that we do not invent.
principled_scan.verdict: No principled (target-blind) minimum on this grid produces the charged-lepton hierarchy.  The Frobenius minimizer is recorded; it is not a unique or physically selected point, and it does not match the lepton ratios.

yukawas.verdict: No principled minimization uniquely fixes the moduli or the lepton ratios.  A labelled 5-parameter fit (plus a discrete Higgs-slice choice) to two observables can accommodate the charged-lepton ratios from some starting points; the system is underdetermined and this is not a prediction.  Other seeds remain far from the target, so the likelihood surface is not a unique well.
